players.product: PMD ICs - FiberEdge TIA/drivers & CopperEdge linear ACC + photonics (gain chips, high-power CW lasers, SOAs, photodiode arrays)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 (call 03-16-2026): record net sales of $274,400,000, up 3% sequentially and up 9% year over year, above the midpoint of the outlook (eighth consecutive quarter of net sales growth); adjusted diluted EPS $0.44, up 10% year over year. Fiscal 2026 net sales a record $1,050,000,000, up 15% year over year, driven by data center and LoRa; FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS $1.71 (+94%). Adjusted gross margin 51.6%; Total Semiconductor Products gross margin 61.7% (up 350 basis points year over year) on favorable LoRa and data center mix.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 net sales $274,400,000 (up 9% year over year); FY2026 net sales $1,050,000,000 (up 15% year over year); Q4 adjusted EPS $0.44; semis GM 61.7%

quarterly_data.signal: DATA CENTER: Q4 net sales a record $63,000,000, up 12% sequentially and up 26% year over year, on record FiberEdge IC sales; Semtech started shipping into LPO transceivers in Q4 (CEO: mid-single-digit, in line with the prior outlook). Fiscal 2026 data center revenues a record $223,000,000, annual growth of 58%. CEO expects data center year-over-year revenue growth this fiscal year (FY2027) to exceed 50%; drivers named: ACC with a hyperscaler, 1.6T FiberEdge in the second half, and possibly linear equalizers onboard (LPO is counted inside FiberEdge). 800G demand 'is the foundation' and stays strong 'at least throughout fiscal 2027' while 1.6T layers on as new XPUs move I/O to 200G.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 DC record $63,000,000 (up 26% year over year); FY2026 DC $223,000,000 (58%); FY2027 DC growth expected to exceed 50%

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2027 OUTLOOK (point-in-time guidance): net sales of $283,000,000 plus or minus $5,000,000 (up 13% year over year at the midpoint); infrastructure up sequentially on projected sequential data center growth of 12%, including initial CopperEdge production shipments supporting a hyperscaler at the tail end of the quarter; adjusted gross margin 52.8% plus or minus 50 basis points; Total Semiconductor Products gross margin 60.4%, down 130 basis points sequentially, including initial ramp costs from the HIFU (as transcribed) acquisition; adjusted EPS $0.45 plus or minus $0.03. CFO: 1.6T copper and optical products ramping in the second half are accretive to Semiconductor and Signal Integrity gross margin, though he is 'not expecting it to be in the sevens'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 FY2027 guide: $283,000,000 plus or minus $5,000,000; data center growth of 12% QoQ; adj GM 52.8%; adj EPS $0.45

quarterly_data.signal: LASER ACQUISITION: Semtech acquired HIFU Corporation (name as printed in this transcript), a California-based maker of indium phosphide optoelectronic devices (gain chips and CW laser chips for optical transceivers), with a comprehensive investment plan for the Alhambra, California facility. Combining its InP lasers with Semtech's TIAs and laser drivers raises Semtech's content opportunity 'from high single-digit dollars in an 800G module to about $80 in a 3.2T module'. The fab is vertically integrated (epi growth, multi-step regrowth, wafer processing, internal test; backend packaging via the ecosystem). The gain chip for tunable lasers is in volume production, capacity limited, and should contribute 'roughly about a high-teen level of revenue' in fiscal 2027. The CW laser for transceivers has 42% wall-plug efficiency at room temperature vs a typical about 25%; there is not enough capacity for industry demand, multiple customers asked for samples, and Semtech plans to intercept at 3.2T transceivers (1.6T also supported). Go-to-market: co-optimized chipsets (TIA, laser driver, modulator driver + lasers) with a reference design; 'the major inflection point is 3.2T transceiver modules. It could be earlier than that.' Deal expected to be accretive to non-GAAP EPS within the first year.
quarterly_data.figure: content from high single-digit dollars (800G) to about $80 in a 3.2T module; CW laser wall-plug efficiency 42% vs about 25% typical

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY: FY2027 priority is supporting customer ramps 'as we compete in a capacity-constrained environment'. For the Alhambra InP fab, CapEx intensity is moderate — it can be supported with about one quarter of free cash flow — but the whole industry is ramping and epi/fab equipment is in high demand, so Semtech will combine new and used equipment; the ramp runs over multiple quarters. CFO: the CapEx should qualify for the Section 48 investment tax credit of 35%, plus other government grant programs. Revenue guidance for CW lasers will come once equipment lead times and capacity are clearer.
quarterly_data.figure: Section 48 investment tax credit of 35%; CapEx about one quarter of free cash flow

quarterly_data.signal: COPPEREDGE / ACC: Semtech expects to start shipping CopperEdge for the 1.6T ACC hyperscaler deployment this quarter — toward the end of the fiscal quarter, in the April time frame, to the cable manufacturers (its direct customers) — to support a rack-level volume ramp in the middle of the year, with demand accelerating through the year; DAC vs ACC mix still being set in rack-level validation. Semtech co-authored the ACC MSA (12 founding members spanning IC, XPU and cable suppliers with major hyperscalers) and says other hyperscalers are 'lining up to get their racks designed by using ACC'. Copper linear equalizers onboard have multiple customer engagements, with customers defining five or six use cases (switch, merchant GPU board, hyperscaler ASIC board, active backplane); qualification expected within the coming quarters. OFC demos: 1.6T ACCs running live traffic to NVIDIA's 224G SerDes and next-generation 448G per-channel CopperEdge chips.
quarterly_data.figure: ACC MSA with 12 founding members; 1.6T ACC shipments start in the April time frame; next-gen 448G per-channel CopperEdge

quarterly_data.signal: LPO / 1.6T FIBEREDGE / NPO: design wins with several leading U.S. hyperscalers validated Semtech TIA and driver solutions in 800G LPO transceivers; 1.6T LPO drivers and TIAs expected to come to market this year; FiberEdge design wins for 1.6T transceivers expected, with a significant ramp in the second half of the year as hyperscalers roll out new XPU and switch platforms using reduced-power 1.6T transceivers. Some hyperscalers are 'increasingly bullish on 1.6T LPO' for the first layer of scale-up fabrics. Semtech is a member of the new XPO MSA (released by Arista) and is developing the NPO (Near Package Optics) MSA with other industry leaders. OFC demos: NVIDIA's 1.6T DR4 transceivers powered by Semtech TIAs and laser drivers running live in NVIDIA's switch platform; a switch on the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 platform running FR4, LR4 and LPO configurations on Semtech silicon; next-generation 448G per-channel modulator drivers and TIAs.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T FiberEdge significant ramp in second half; 448G per-channel modulator drivers and TIAs demoed

quarterly_data.signal: CEO VIEW ON COPPER VS CPO: 'Copper scale-up is always going to be there, and CPO scale-up is only going to make more sense in multirack systems' (e.g. NVL576 across eight racks, NVL1152); copper scale-up stays mainstream within a rack — 'do not put a terminal value on copper yet'. NPO is a complement to CPO that leverages the whole ecosystem: 'In CPO, we may not have much content in there except for lasers. But in NPO, we will be all over the place—with laser drivers, TIAs, and lasers, and even silicon photonics modulators'.

connects_to.relationship: TIAs and laser drivers in NVIDIA 1.6T DR4 optical transceivers
